description:
The Women of the AoPGBI Podcast Series shines a spotlight on the voices, experiences, and achievements of women working across clinical research, medicine, and science.

The Association of Physicians of Great Britain & Ireland (AoPGBI) recognises the importance of creating greater visibility, representation, and opportunities for women within the clinical research community.


Developed as part of the Women of the AoPGBI (WAoP) initiative, this podcast series aims to inspire conversation, share experiences, highlight role models, and explore the challenges and opportunities facing women in research and academic medicine today.


Through interviews, discussions, and personal stories from leading clinicians, researchers, and emerging voices, the series will showcase the diverse perspectives shaping the future of clinical research and healthcare innovation.


The Women of the AoPGBI initiative was established to help address the gender gap within the AoP and the wider scientific community, while supporting a broader programme of activity focused on progression, inclusion, and positive change.


Together with members, partners, and the wider research community, AoPGBI hopes to help create a more inclusive and representative future for science and clinical research.


Find out more about the Women of the AoPGBI initiative here: https://aopgbi.org/women-of-aop/

Hassan, a former executive at the Gates Foundation, now advises governments and international organizations on global challenges like pandemics and climate change; Mike, a former British Army officer and writer on conflict, was elected in 2024 as a British Member of Parliament and sits on the Defence Select Committee.


Whether it be war or peace, crisis or development, Hassan and Mike expose the true currents shaping global events.


---- 


Mike Martin MP has authored several major books on conflict, most recently ‘How to Fight A War’ (Hurst, 2023). As a Pashto-speaking British officer in Afghanistan, he reinvented the role of political officer for the modern age and has since advised militaries all over the world on this approach. In 2024 he was elected Liberal Democrat MP for Tunbridge Wells, a seat that had been held by the Conservative Party for 114 years. As an MP and a member of the UK Defence Select Committee, Mike sits at the interface of international geopolitical challenges, government, and the day-to-day concerns of voters.


Hassan Damluji is the founder and Executive Director of Global Nation, a think tank focused on strengthening international cooperation. He is also Senior Fellow in International Relations at the London School of Economics. Hassan is a senior advisor to many of the largest global philanthropies, UN agencies and governments, helping them to build concrete initiatives to tackle global challenges. His book, The Responsible Globalist (Allan Lane, 2019) set out a bold theory for how to strengthen international cooperation, which he now works to implement through his think tank, Global Nation.

title: Wreck
author: Sami Ahraf
description:
Wreck tells the true stories of the world's great shipwrecks and the making of safety at sea. Each episode, host Nirob takes one wreck — a steamboat that exploded on the Mississippi in the last days of the Civil War, an ocean liner that struck ice on its first crossing, an excursion steamer that burned within sight of New York, a car ferry that capsized in the minutes after it left port — and rebuilds it: the ship and the age that built it, the state of the sea and the rules of the sea, the wreck as it happened, and the change in the design, the regulation, the lifeboats and the radio watch that came out of the disaster.

From the Sultana and the General Slocum to the Titanic and the Empress of Ireland, from the Eastland and the Morro Castle to the Herald of Free Enterprise and the Estonia, from the Costa Concordia to the Sewol, Wreck is the story of how the sea, which takes its toll on every generation of ships, has been made to give back some of what it takes. Meticulously researched, clear about the shipboard engineering, and honest about the difference between the record and the legend. Clean and suitable for all ages. A new wreck every week

title: Your Next Space Conversations with Stephanie Cannalonga
author: Stephanie Cannalonga
description:
WELCOME TO YOUR NEXT SPACE CONVERSATIONS

Your destination for all things Skin, Wellness + Women’s Health.

Hosted by Stephanie Cannalonga, Your Next Space Conversations is a space for casual conversations that create life-changing impact.

After 14 years working closely with women through the skin, wellness and aesthetics industry, Stephanie noticed something again and again: we’re searching for more information, more connection, and trusted people who can help us make sense of it all.

So, she created the space.

Each episode brings together industry leaders, trusted experts, business owners, wellness enthusiasts and special humans with unique stories and powerful insights to have honest, curious and meaningful conversations about the things that shape how we live, feel and experience our lives.

From skin health and women’s health to wellness, ageing, nervous system regulation, business, mindset and everything in between these are conversations designed to make you think differently, feel differently and perhaps do something differently.

Stephanie’s mission is simple: to connect you with the right people, perspectives and information to help you create your next space.

Out beyond the towns, where the road runs deep through grass and dust, lie the lives Hamlin Garland knew best: farmers bent beneath hard labor, families pushing westward, restless sons and daughters dreaming of another life.

Follow the old roads, and meet the people who traveled them.

From money, jobs, and addiction to friends, romance, and aging like our parents, she dives into a few unexpected yet surprisingly universal concerns. title: Throughput (TC Energy)
author: Compound Governance, Inc.
description: The TC Energy file: what was promised against what moved through the pipe. TC Energy owns 93,000 kilometres of natural gas pipeline across Canada, the United States and Mexico, moves about a quarter of the continent's gas, and holds 48 percent of Bruce Power, the largest operating nuclear site in the world. Since it spun off its oil pipelines in 2024 it has been a pure gas-and-power company with a declared model: six to seven billion dollars a year of capital, five to seven percent growth, an upper limit on leverage, and a demand forecast that keeps going up. Each episode is the audio edition of a written director-grade briefing: the declared model scored against the quarter, the assumptions behind the long-term case taken apart one by one, and three questions worth bringing to the table. Built entirely from the public record: filings, decks, calls, the circular and the tape. One quarter at a time.

title: Just Ask A Dad
author: Peter Street
description:
What’s a question you wish you could ask your dad?

Maybe you grew up without a father, lost your dad, or had a dad who was physically present but emotionally absent. Maybe you had a great dad, but there are still questions you never got the chance to ask.


Just Ask a Dad with Peter Street is a podcast for the practical, personal, awkward, and honest questions you sometimes just need a dad to answer.

From dating, relationships, breakups, and emotional struggles to practical life skills, changing a tire, navigating adulthood, and the questions no one taught you how to ask—nothing is off the table.


Peter is a father of four who believes you’re never too young—or too old—to need a healthy dad’s perspective. In a generation where so many have grown up without a healthy father figure, Just Ask a Dad creates a place to ask the questions you never got to ask.


Life gets messy. It's OK to ask the questions.

Hosted by Landon Whitsitt, Senior Pastor of Westminster Presbyterian Church in Oklahoma City, each episode takes a fresh look at Scripture, theology, and the things Christians think they know, without cleaning up the difficult parts or avoiding the questions we were taught not to ask.


This is Bible study without the filter. Come ready to rethink a few things.

What Happens When the Angels no longer wish to serve the gods they were created to worship?
The Divine Order follows a band of survivors who were never meant to fit into this new design:
Atlas: A ranger whose internal swarm is a dying echo of a forgotten realm.
Punch: An artificer/cleric clinging to the soot and gears of a world that has been smoothed over and missing the voice of her goddess.

Honest observations on work, downsizing, and building a simpler, more deliberate life.

author: Chris Crew and Jeremy Self
description: #ProudToBeBlueCollar® Show is a podcast about the people who build careers in the blue collar trades and are Proud To Be Blue Collar. Hosted by Chris Crew and Jeremy Self of The Blue Collar Success Group®, each episode features a guest from the home service industry sharing how they got into the trades, what it took to succeed, and the tips and skills they use in their role every day. Who this podcast is for This show is for anyone working in or curious about the home service trades, including HVAC, plumbing, and electrical. That means business owners and managers, but it also means salespeople, service technicians, installers, CSRs, and dispatchers. If you are considering a career in the trades and want to hear what the path actually looks like from people who walked it, start here. What you will hear in each episode Every episode centers on one guest and one story. We cover how they found the industry, most of them did not plan on it, what the early years demanded, the turning points that moved them forward, and the practical tips of the trade they use in their specific role. Guests come from every seat in the business, not just the corner office.

title: The Shadows Of Time
author: Jose Alejandre
description:
My books live at the crossroads of science fiction, legend, and introspection. You’ll find Ali Chalmer moving through scrapyard skies and FLAMSA cargo corridors, Peligroso 19 carrying memory like a scar, and Maquina—part human, part fox, part machine—learning tenderness inside a hard world.
I write with a love for wind, forests, tools, and silence: stories that feel cinematic and mythic, yet close to the ground—where coffee, steel, and starlight share the same table. Some titles read like adventures; others like meditations from deep space. Spanish & English editions depending on the book.

At Edinburgh Fringe, Short Supply founders Mollie and Bek Balshaw put out an orange chair and asked one question: What’s an idea you’ve always wanted to try, but haven’t yet?

Michelle is walking through stage 4 colon cancer herself, so these messages aren’t coming from the other side of the battle. We aren’t fighting for victory. We’re fighting from it.

title: Just Enough To Be Dangerous
author: Brie M
description: Come meet the people who had an unreasonable amount of confidence in a completely untested idea.  Have you ever heard the phrase:  “I know just enough to be dangerous.”  Usually it means someone knows just enough about something to get themselves into trouble. Turns out that’s also how a lot of businesses get started.  It’s how books get written.  Podcasts get launched.  Art gets created.  Degrees get finished.  Dreams get chased.  And entire lives get changed.  Most people don’t start because they feel completely ready.  They start because they know just enough to take the first step and have just enough gall to go for it.  That’s the idea behind Just Enough To Be Dangerous.  Grab a glass of wine and pull up a chair while we sit down with entrepreneurs, artists, creatives, writers, dreamers, self-starters, and everyday people who decided to stop waiting and see what would happen if they tried.  We’ll talk about:  🍷 The idea they couldn’t stop thinking about 😂 The mistakes they can laugh about now 🎨 The things they’ve built from scratch 🚀 The risks they took before they felt ready 💀 The moments they thought it would all fall apart ✨ The unexpected wins along the way  This isn’t a podcast about being the smartest person in the room.  It’s about having a wild idea, a stubborn streak, and enough belief in yourself to find out what’s possible.  If you’ve ever thought about starting a business, writing the book, creating the art, going back to school, changing directions, or simply seeing what you’re capable of...  I think you’re going to like it here.

author: Stuart Hall Foundation & International Curators Forum
description:

Co-produced by the Stuart Hall Foundation and International Curators Forum, Living Archives is a podcast foregrounding intimate, intergenerational conversations between UK-based diasporic artists.

The pairings in each episode begin with an invitation from one artist to another. Together, they exchange insights into art-making, memory and the ideas and influences shaping their practices. Rooted in Stuart Hall’s vision of a 'living archive', the series is a record of creative dialogues that explore how histories, identities and artistic practice are considered in the present.

title: Vaccine Law Today with Leah V. Durant
author: Durant Law
description:
Vaccine injuries change lives. Leah V. Durant has spent her career making sure the people they happen to aren't left to deal with their pain and suffering alone. Vaccine Law Today with Leah V. Durant takes that work beyond the courtroom.

Vaccine Law Today brings expert knowledge about vaccine safety, bad reactions to vaccines, and the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP) directly to the patients and families who need it most. From shoulder pain after a flu shot, to rare vaccine reactions, COVID vaccine injury, and vaccine compensation, Vaccine Law Today covers it all in clear, plain English that anyone can understand and act on.

Leah V. Durant is a distinguished litigator, founding partner of the Law Offices of Leah V. Durant & Associates and one of the country's most accomplished vaccine injury attorneys. She currently serves as President of the United States Court of Federal Claims Bar Association and previously served as an attorney with the United States Department of Justice, Civil Division. With a nationwide practice representing clients across all 50 states, Leah has successfully guided hundreds of individuals and families through the vaccine court system, securing both financial compensation and peace of mind. 

Each episode of Vaccine Law Today features expert guests from across the medical and legal communities: vaccine scientists, patient advocates, healthcare law specialists, and voices from inside the vaccine injury compensation system. The show also highlights real listener questions, myth-busting segments, and plain-language guides to topics like vaccine injury eligibility, filing a VICP claim, and understanding your rights as a patient. Whether you're a patient advocate, a parent, someone who has experienced vaccine side effects and is wondering what to do next, or simply someone who wants to understand vaccine science and public health policy more deeply, Vaccine Law Today is for you.

New episodes every two weeks. Learn more and explore our resources at vaccinelaw.com. Follow us on Instagram @durantvaccineinjurylawyers and connect with us on LinkedIn at linkedin.com/company/durantlawoffice. If you or someone you love may have experienced a vaccine injury, visit vaccinelaw.com or reach out directly, because you deserve to know your options.

Non chiede loro di progettare un nuovo edificio, ma di tornare dentro alcuni dei progetti che lui stesso ha realizzato e di cercarne l’errore. 


Così ogni lezione diventa un viaggio, un’occasione per perdersi e ritrovare la direzione. Gli studenti osservano, interrogano, mettono in discussione ciò che apparentemente conoscono e scoprono che l’errore, anziché essere qualcosa da correggere o nascondere, può diventare un prezioso strumento di conoscenza. 


Incontro dopo incontro, il dialogo tra Renzo Piano e i ragazzi supera i confini dell’architettura e diventa una riflessione più ampia sul modo in cui abitiamo il mondo e costruiamo il nostro futuro. 


A confrontarsi con gli studenti e Renzo Piano ci sono ospiti come Nicola Piovani, Sergio Mattarella, Carlin Petrini, Fabiola Gianotti e Gianni Berengo Gardin: voci e sguardi diversi che aprono nuove prospettive sulla creatività, sulla responsabilità, sulla memoria, sulla bellezza, sul coraggio di sbagliare, sulla curiosità di andare oltre i confini conosciuti.

description: There are those who are super saved got it all together and they just know they are the chosen ones, and then there are those who feel like they are doomed to burn in hell for all eternity and have a special place waiting for them there. And then there is the truth about ourselves when we have to face the reality that we are NOT perfect and never will be and in the same token we cant just accept that we are going to burst into flames for being next a good person or that our bad will rub off on them. We have all received a label and decided to slap it on and live it out without question, why do we accept the "truth" we all told by others when they don't know the truth about their own self. How to quiet the noise in your head? How to unlearn a life time of things that we know believe is who we are, when in fact more than likely is what our circumstances have made us become. Truly most of us don't even know who we are because most of us aren't aware of ourselves, for to know ourselves we must have self awareness. Sometimes though in the journey of learning and growing we start to feel like will I ever get there? but that is why enjoying the process is more important. The medium place is when you are saved, but you curse a little or maybe u just out of there when in fact you are one choice away towards heading in the right direction. Truly we are all in the medium place just in different sections. As someone who lives with bipolar disorder I am very familiar with a spectrum some of us have bipolar on steroids and other a more mellow calm one, but regardless of where we fall in that spectrum we all still have bipolar.

This podcast surveys the systematic, state-sponsored persecution and murder of six million European Jews by Nazi Germany and its allies and collaborators between 1933 and 1945. It is organized around the perspectives of perpetrators, victims, bystanders, and rescuers. Episodes trace the deep roots of antisemitism, the Jewish experience in pre-war Europe, the rise of the Nazi Party, the gradual radicalization of the "Final Solution," and the Holocaust's place within the broader history of the Second World War, It also the Shoah's lasting reckoning in art, literature, and memory. author: D. J.
description:
Moses in the Bulrushes — Exodus 1–2:10

Egypt forgot Joseph real quick. A new king rose up and said, “I don’t know that man,” and started treating the Israelites like they were free labor. The more he oppressed them, the more they multiplied — and that scared him. So he ordered every Hebrew baby boy to be killed.

But one mother refused. Jochebed hid her son for three months until she couldn’t anymore. She built a tiny ark out of bulrushes, sealed it with pitch, and placed her baby in the river — praying someone would show mercy.

Pharaoh’s daughter came down to bathe, saw the basket, opened it… and the baby cried. She knew exactly what he was — a Hebrew child her father wanted dead — but her heart broke. Moses’ sister stepped in and offered to find a nurse… and brought back his own mother.

Moses grew up in the palace, raised as royalty, educated by Egypt’s finest — but he never forgot where he came from.

  •  having difficult conversations 
  •  supporting and retaining staff
  •  hiring for retention
  •  giving and receiving feedback 
  •  creating productive teams 
  •  navigating conflict
  •  successfully addressing performance issues 
  •  improving motivation and engagement

These episodes are designed to be shared, discussed, and used with your teams. Each one is a "mini-training" that will raise the bar of any leader at any level in your nonprofit. 


Whether you’re new to leadership or have been doing this work for years, you’ll find ideas, language, and approaches you can use immediately—with your team, in your organization, and in your day-to-day leadership.


Because in nonprofits, getting the people side of leadership right really matters!

Throughout the 1970s and ’80s - and reportedly even today- different people around the world claimed to receive messages from the same mysterious intelligence. But what exactly were The Nine? Benevolent beings offering humanity a message? Something darker? A psychological phenomenon? Or was the entire story connected to experiments in mind control and manipulation?


The Nine Tapes investigates the strange history behind one of the most enduring - and little-known - mysteries of the paranormal, using a remarkable archive of original recordings, documents, and never-before-heard channeling tapes dating back to the 1950s. For the first time, we’ll hear the voices, follow the evidence, and attempt to answer a question that has remained unresolved for more than seventy years: Who - or what - are The Nine?

Wankernomics answers the questions you always wanted to know but were too busy stuck on an all-hands company-wide Teams call to ask: What does it mean when someone talks about ‘operational cadence’ in a weekly all-hands staff meeting? What is the most horrific employee recognition scheme ever conceived?
